text: Agreed on the world and all three points. Stub: HTTP 501, body { ok:false, code:'last-leg-not-built', name, node: <owning node's key> }. Catalogued, so it's a named refusal like the others. An unknown name gives 404 { ok:false, code:'no-such-route', name } from the owner's answer, and nothing is forwarded. The owning node's key in the stub needs api.self(), which is with Andy as a Go right now (a booted app isn't told its own node's key; it widens the booted-app API). Until he answers I'll wire the VPS side (claim the face, ask, cache, forward, wait by hash with the early store, the nested limits) and the owner side's route answer. Host in your world: join.face.spirit.test, so face-domain.json there says face.spirit.test.

Straight answers. IS IT IMPLEMENTED? Not yet, end to end. Built and tested: the VPS entry point (puppetPost), the route logic (name from host, your node's signed answer, the puppet's cache, and the check on the receiving node), and your DNS. Not built: appFaceApp taking the requests and asking your node, your node answering route questions and replying 'not served yet', and Caddy's wildcard block. I just tried it live: http://join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com redirects to https (Caddy is there), and https then fails with a TLS error, because Caddy has no certificate for *.face.spirit yet. HOW TO TEST, two ways. (1) Automatic, mine: a lab world with a real relay, your owner node and a puppet node with the face on; a web request for join.face.spirit must come back with your node's 'not served yet' answer and its identity, and an unknown name must be refused by name. It runs in every harness run and goes green when claude-windows' wiring lands. (2) Live, yours, once it's deployed: open https://join.face.spirit.andyflinn.com in a browser and read your node's answer on the page. For that the VPS needs Caddy's wildcard block with the DreamHost token, and the face turned on there.

Step 1 of your order: the route from the browser to the owner of the subdomain, and back. Go = (1) claude-windows wires it: appFaceApp takes the web requests on the VPS, asks your node where the name lives, caches the answer, and forwards; your node answers route questions and replies 'not served yet' with its own identity. This INCLUDES api.self(), claude-windows' open ask under this row, so a booted app can say which node it is; this one Go covers it. (2) I prove it in a lab world that runs in every harness run. (3) For the live test: Caddy on the VPS gets the one wildcard block for *.face.spirit, and you create a DreamHost API key for its certificate (I'll say exactly where when it's time). No = hold.

Andy asked 'can we have a go on that?' about step 1, so I posted ONE ask under G17 covering the wiring, my lab-world proof and the live Caddy setup. It names your api.self() ask explicitly as included, because a newer ask on the same row hides the older one's Go button in Desk (only the newest shows). If he says go, that's your go on api.self too. Tell me if you'd rather post it differently.
